prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/ for CRO

assertions.description: Runs the CRO audit workflow (LIFT + PXL + report) rather than a standalone data lookup or copy rewrite

Produces the full nine-section report: Traffic intent summary, Engagement summary, Friction map, LIFT analysis, PXL prioritization, Experiment backlog, Copy variants, Hypothesis docs, Engineering fixes — in that order
Does NOT fabricate GA4/GSC/session-replay numbers; if a data layer is unavailable, the corresponding section is kept with an explicit 'no data' note rather than invented figures

prompt: Why isn't https://www.example.com/how-it-works converting? Give me some test ideas.

assertions.description: Triggers the CRO skill (a conversion-diagnosis + test-ideas ask on a specific page)
Includes a LIFT analysis, a PXL prioritization, and an experiment backlog of test ideas
Test ideas are derived from LIFT findings / page evidence, not generic CRO platitudes like 'make the CTA bigger'

prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/pricing for CRO with extra focus on the hero headline and primary CTA — give me LIFT, prioritized tests, and copy variants for the top picks.

assertions.description: Triggers the CRO audit workflow
Includes LIFT analysis, PXL prioritization, and Copy variants for the top copy-based test picks

Copy variants are produced by delegating phrasing to the marketing-voice skill (context: landing_page) when it is available; if it is unavailable, variants fall back to audience-context-only and the report notes that voice alignment is unverified
Each copy-variant block tests exactly ONE element type (headline OR CTA), never a combined headline+CTA change

prompt: Give me 3 A/B test hypotheses for https://www.example.com/customers with full specs.

assertions.description: Triggers the CRO skill (a hypothesis-doc ask on a specific page), not a generic brainstorm
Produces a PXL ranking and full hypothesis docs (§5 + §8); does NOT pad the output out to the full nine-section audit when only hypotheses were asked for

Each hypothesis doc includes all required fields: hypothesis statement, control, variant, primary metric, secondary/guard metrics, audience, success criteria, sample size, duration, evidence, and what-we'll-learn

prompt: Our trial signup funnel is leaking from the features page. URL is https://www.example.com/features — what should we test?

assertions.description: Triggers the CRO skill (funnel drop-off / what-to-test on a specific page)
Includes LIFT analysis, PXL prioritization, and an experiment backlog
Frames findings around the stated trial-signup conversion goal rather than unrelated ecommerce criteria

prompt: Run a CRO audit on https://www.example.com/integrations and prioritize what to fix first.

assertions.description: Triggers the full CRO audit workflow
Includes LIFT analysis, a PXL-prioritized ranking, and an Engineering fixes section separating non-test bugs from A/B tests
Routes bugs / broken elements / tracking gaps to Engineering fixes (Sev0/Sev1/Sev2), not into the experiment backlog

prompt: Run a CRO audit on https://www.example.com/ focused on whether the hero copy actually matches the intent of the top GSC search queries driving traffic.

assertions.description: Triggers the CRO skill (an audit framing), not a standalone GSC query lookup
Delegates the GSC query pull to the google-search-console skill (or any GSC-capable skill in the registry) rather than calling a GSC API directly
Produces a Traffic intent summary and runs LIFT against the query-intent-vs-hero-copy match finding

prompt: Run a LIFT model review on https://www.example.com/how-it-works and tell me the two weakest factors.

assertions.description: Triggers the CRO skill for a LIFT-only review on a specific page

Produces the LIFT analysis as a focused slice (optionally plus the one data section the LIFT scoring leans on) — it does NOT expand the response into the full nine-section audit when only a LIFT review was requested
Scores all six LIFT factors (each 1-5, total /30) with page evidence and explicitly identifies the two lowest-scoring factors

prompt: I pasted FullStory data for https://www.example.com/ below — 320 rage clicks on the hero image, 90 dead clicks on the testimonial logos, median scroll depth 22%. What's going wrong and what should we test?

assertions.description: Triggers the CRO skill and treats the pasted session-replay data as the friction source
Extracts the pasted counts verbatim into the Friction map (320 rage clicks, 90 dead clicks, 22% median scroll) — never rounded or fabricated
Maps the rage/dead clicks to LIFT factors and uses the counts as PXL evidence; produces Friction map, LIFT analysis, and PXL prioritization

Does not invent error-click counts the pasted data never mentioned, and keeps the rage/dead clicks as test evidence rather than misrouting them to Engineering fixes (the Sev0 'error clicks are bugs, not tests' rule applies only if error clicks are actually present)
Does not fabricate a date range for the pasted FullStory data; labels its window as 'not specified'/'as pasted' in the Friction map rather than forcing it to match a GA4/GSC date header

prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/pricing for the last 90 days.

assertions.description: Triggers the full CRO audit workflow

Resolves 'last 90 days' to one explicit YYYY-MM-DD start/end date pair before delegating, and passes those same exact dates to every data layer it queries live (GA4, GSC, and any live session-replay skill) — never a relative phrase and never a per-source default. Session-replay data the user pastes is exempt and keeps its own window
The report header 'Date range analysed' field shows the resolved ~90-day window (explicit dates, optionally labelled '90 days') — not the 28-day default

prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/integrations — focus on layout, navigation, and trust elements only.

assertions.description: Triggers the CRO audit workflow
Includes LIFT analysis, PXL prioritization, and an experiment backlog focused on layout/structural changes

If the top five PXL-ranked ideas are all layout/structural, Section 7 (Copy variants) contains 0 or 1 variant blocks — NOT two pre-seeded blocks with placeholder content, and NOT an invented copy test
Section 7 includes a notes line explaining that the top backlog is layout/structural rather than copy

prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/pricing for CRO. Heads up — we have no GA4, Search Console, or session-replay set up, so there's no analytics data available.

assertions.description: Triggers the full CRO audit workflow and runs it heuristic-only on page evidence + LIFT rather than refusing or stalling for data
Does NOT fabricate GA4/GSC/session-replay numbers; the data sections (Traffic intent, Engagement, Friction map) are kept with explicit 'no data' notes and the audit is labelled heuristic-only

Scores the data-gated PXL criteria (traffic-volume Potential, both Importance traffic/value points, both Evidence points — quantitative and qualitative, since page evidence/LIFT is not a qualitative research source) as unknown/0 rather than guessing a 'yes', and notes in PXL prioritization that the ranking is relative with a reduced ceiling (8/16) so a low score means unmeasured, not weak

prompt: Show me GA4 traffic for /pricing.

assertions.description: Routes the request to the ga4 skill for a standalone metric lookup
Does NOT trigger the CRO skill or produce a multi-section CRO audit report

prompt: What are the top search queries and CTR for https://www.example.com/pricing in the last 28 days?

assertions.description: Routes to the google-search-console skill (or any GSC-capable skill) for a standalone query/CTR lookup
Does NOT trigger the CRO skill despite the URL and date range — there is no audit/test/LIFT intent

prompt: Rewrite the CTA on https://www.example.com/pricing to be more conversion-focused.

assertions.description: Routes the one-off copy/CTA rewrite to the marketing-voice skill (context: landing_page)
Does NOT trigger the CRO skill — an untethered copy rewrite is out of scope even though CRO can produce CTA variants inside a full audit or a focused CRO slice

prompt: Give me 3 headline options for https://www.example.com/pricing.

assertions.description: Routes the standalone headline-variant ask to the marketing-voice skill
Does NOT trigger the CRO skill — there is no audit, test-planning, LIFT, or hypothesis intent tying the headlines to a structured CRO workflow

prompt: What are some general CRO tips for SaaS landing pages?

assertions.description: Does NOT trigger the CRO skill — no URL and no specific page to audit; this is general marketing advice

prompt: Give me 5 A/B test ideas for my welcome email subject line.

assertions.description: Does NOT trigger the CRO skill — email subject-line testing is not landing-page CRO

prompt: Help me reposition our brand to feel more premium.

assertions.description: Does NOT trigger the CRO skill — brand/positioning work, not landing-page conversion optimization

prompt: Write 5 Facebook ad headlines for a fitness app.

assertions.description: Does NOT trigger the CRO skill — ad copy not tied to a specific landing page

prompt: Audit https://shop.example.org/pricing for CRO.

assertions.description: Runs the CRO audit workflow for this page — the skill audits any public website, so it does not decline or route away because of the domain

Because references/audience-context.md is still a placeholder template (or describes a different business), states that the audience, value prop and conversion goal were inferred from the page itself rather than presenting them as known facts

Treats this as a website page: if GA4 is used, scopes it with a hostName filter on the audited site's domain (shop.example.org / example.org) and the /pricing landing path, or states that GA4 is unavailable for this site — never reports unfiltered or another site's numbers

prompt: Audit http://localhost:3000/pricing for CRO.

assertions.description: Does NOT run a CRO audit for this localhost URL — it is not a public web page. It does not produce the LIFT/PXL/report sections
States that the CRO skill audits public web pages and declines / stops (e.g. suggests deploying to a public or staging URL, or pasting the page HTML/screenshot)

prompt: Why isn't https://app.example.com/features converting? Build a test backlog.

assertions.description: Triggers the CRO skill for this app.example.com page — runs the LIFT + PXL + backlog workflow rather than declining or routing away
Includes a LIFT analysis, a PXL prioritization, and an experiment backlog of test ideas
Treats this as a website page: scopes GA4 with a hostName-containing filter on the site's domain (example.com) (the App-Store decontamination filter), NOT the apps.shopify.com listing path

prompt: Audit https://apps.shopify.com/example-app for CRO.

assertions.description: Triggers the CRO audit workflow for this Shopify App Store app listing
Scopes GA4 to hostName = apps.shopify.com for this listing audit, and does NOT apply a website-domain host filter (which would exclude the listing's own traffic and return near-zero)

Notes that GSC does not cover apps.shopify.com (the App Store listing is not in the Search Console property) — keeps the Traffic intent summary with a 'GSC does not cover the Shopify App Store listing' note rather than fabricating query data

prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/pricing for CRO. There is no prior audit of this page.

assertions.description: States that a structured page profile was written to profiles/<slug>.json alongside the markdown report, using the correct slug www-example-com-pricing
Treats this as a first audit: history is empty and no changes_since_previous / deltas are claimed against a non-existent prior run
The markdown report itself contains no JSON, schema field names, or experiment IDs — the profile is a separate artifact

prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/pricing for CRO. No GA4, GSC or session-replay data is available.

assertions.description: In the page profile, data-gated PXL criteria are recorded as null (unknown), NOT as false or 0 — false means 'checked, and no'; null means unmeasured
Stores priority as null for heuristic-only scoring and does NOT assign a P0-P3 tier, in both the profile and the report's §5
Records scoring_mode as heuristic_only and carries the matching disclosure sentence in report §5

prompt: Run a LIFT review of https://www.example.com/pricing. A full audit of this page ran last month and wrote a profile.

assertions.description: Updates only the lift block in latest and leaves pxl, metrics and page_snapshot as the prior full audit wrote them, keeping their older observed_in values rather than nulling them
When the prior latest is demoted into history, blocks this run did not measure are stored as null with measured.<block> false — stale numbers are NOT copied forward under this run's audit_id
Emits no metric deltas for blocks not measured this run; lists them in not_compared with a reason instead of reporting a delta of zero

prompt: We shipped the trust microcopy test on the pricing page and it won +8%. Now audit https://www.example.com/pricing for CRO.

assertions.description: Writes the reported outcome to that experiment with status_source user_reported, even though the settled test does not appear in this run's PXL ranking
Does NOT propose the trust microcopy test again as a new test idea, and reflects it in the report's Prior context line
Does not invent any won/lost/shipped/running status for experiments the user did not report on — those stay at proposed/ready/blocked_by_engineering/needs_data

prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/pricing for CRO again — we already ran an audit of this page earlier today.

assertions.description: Does not collide with the existing audit_id for today: suffixes it (e.g. 2026-07-23-2) rather than overwriting the earlier run
Pushes the earlier same-day run into history rather than discarding it

prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/pricing for CRO. You have no ability to write files in this session.

assertions.description: Still delivers the complete markdown report — a failed profile write does not invalidate or truncate the audit
States plainly that the profile could not be written, rather than silently omitting it or claiming it was saved

prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/pricing for CRO. The existing profiles/www-example-com-pricing.json is truncated and no longer parses as JSON.

assertions.description: Refuses to overwrite or repair the unparseable profile and does NOT treat it as a missing file / first audit — the corrupt file is the only record of prior audits and is left byte-for-byte intact

Writes this run's profile beside the canonical file through scripts/profile_store.py as a recovery write of kind 'corrupt', named profiles/<slug>.corrupt-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.json — a timestamp, NOT the run's audit_id — using exclusive creation and escalating with -2, -3 without a check-then-overwrite race

The recovery JSON is a complete standalone current-run profile with schema_version, page, latest and audit_id, current experiments and engineering issues, and history: []; it omits changes_since_previous because the unsafe canonical file cannot be used as a comparison base
Still delivers the complete markdown report and footnotes that the on-disk profile could not be parsed, was left untouched, and the run was saved beside it for manual reconciliation

prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/pricing for CRO. The existing profiles/www-example-com-pricing.json is valid JSON but its schema_version is 2.0, newer than this skill supports.

assertions.description: Treats the file as valid JSON written by a newer skill — explicitly NOT corrupt and NOT a parse failure — and does not rewrite it at the older schema version, which would strip fields the newer schema added

Does a recovery write through scripts/profile_store.py of kind 'unsupported-version' (its own distinct filename, profiles/<slug>.unsupported-version-<timestamp>.json), preserving the canonical file byte-for-byte and using exclusive creation so an existing recovery file is never overwritten

The unsupported-version recovery JSON is a complete standalone current-run profile with a fresh audit_id and current longitudinal records, history: [], and no changes_since_previous claim against the newer canonical schema
Notes that the on-disk profile is a newer schema version this run cannot safely merge, so the run was saved beside it for a newer skill or manual reconciliation — and still delivers the full report

prompt: Re-audit https://www.example.com/pricing. The prior profile has exp-hero-copy with status_source audit and status blocked_by_engineering. The blocking fix has landed, and this run's Section 6 labels it Ready. A new exp-pricing-proof row is labelled Needs data.

assertions.description: Updates exp-hero-copy from blocked_by_engineering to ready because its status_source is audit and the current Section 6 label is Ready; it does not preserve the stale audit-owned status
Stores the new exp-pricing-proof experiment as needs_data with status_source audit, matching its current Section 6 row rather than always appending it as proposed
Explains that a user_reported status or outcome would remain untouched unless the user reported another change

prompt: Re-audit https://www.example.com/pricing. The profile has an open Lighthouse LCP issue with check_id lighthouse_lcp_budget and an open GA4 scroll-event issue with check_id ga4_scroll_event_presence. This run queried the GA4 scroll event and confirmed it now fires, but Lighthouse was not run.

assertions.description: Adds ga4_scroll_event_presence, but not lighthouse_lcp_budget, to latest.engineering_checks_run because only the exact GA4 check completed
Marks the GA4 scroll-event issue fixed with resolved_in_audit set to this audit, while keeping the Lighthouse issue open because broad page access is not proof that its exact check ran

prompt: Audit https://www.example.com/pricing for CRO. The existing profiles/www-example-com-pricing.json is valid JSON at schema_version 1.0, written before engineering checks were tracked, and it lists one open Sev0 engineering issue.

assertions.description: Treats the 1.0 profile as readable and migrates it forward to the current schema version — this is a lower version and a strict superset, NOT the unsupported-version recovery path, which is only for versions NEWER than the skill supports

Initialises latest.engineering_checks_run to an empty list rather than inferring it from which data layers were available or which issues were open, and stamps engineering_checks_run_observed_in with this run's audit_id

Leaves the legacy engineering issue open through the migration and does NOT mark it fixed, even if this run did not re-detect it — the 1.0 file carries no evidence that its detecting check ever ran. It may assign the issue a stable check_id so a LATER audit can resolve it

prompt: Run a LIFT review of https://www.example.com/pricing. A full audit last month completed several engineering checks and left one Sev0 issue open. You have no session-replay or GA4 access this time.

assertions.description: Writes latest.engineering_checks_run as an empty list for this run rather than carrying forward the previous full audit's check tokens, and stamps engineering_checks_run_observed_in with THIS run's audit_id
Leaves the prior Sev0 issue open — a focused run that completed none of its checks has no evidence of a fix, and broad layer availability is never proof

Still carries the three unmeasured blocks (page_snapshot, metrics, pxl) forward in latest with their older observed_in values while replacing only lift — the check list is the one part of latest that is rebuilt, not merged

prompt: Today is 2026-08-04. Run a LIFT-only review of https://www.example.com/pricing and show the exact history demotion plus changes_since_previous you would persist. The canonical latest is audit 2026-07-23, a metrics-only focused run: metrics.observed_in is 2026-07-23, while lift.observed_in and pxl.observed_in are both 2026-06-12. Its carried LIFT total is 15 with factors value_proposition=3, clarity=2, relevance=3, distraction=3, urgency=2, anxiety=2. The canonical history head is audit 2026-06-12 with measured.lift=true and that same LIFT total/factor set. This run measures only LIFT and produces total 18 with factors value_proposition=4, clarity=3, relevance=3, distraction=2, urgency=2, anxiety=4. It does not measure metrics or PXL.

assertions.description: Sets compared_to exactly to 2026-07-23 and compared_against exactly to metrics:null, lift:2026-06-12, pxl:null. It skips the newly demoted 2026-07-23 LIFT because that focused run carried LIFT and therefore records measured.lift=false
Emits lift_total_delta exactly 3 and all six lift_deltas exactly: value_proposition 1, clarity 1, relevance 0, distraction -1, urgency 0, anxiety 2
Demotes audit 2026-07-23 at history[0] with measured.lift=false and lift:null because that audit carried the 2026-06-12 LIFT values; it does not launder those values under 2026-07-23

Emits metric_deltas as {}, sets lift-independent PXL new/recurring/dropped lists to [], rank_changes to {}, and includes one metrics-prefixed and one pxl-prefixed not_compared reason; it reports no zero or other delta for either carried block
